title: Alex Hormozi on opportunity, niching, skills and brand: lessons from Gym Launch's near-collapse
summary: Hormozi tells how Gym Launch nearly collapsed, then recovered by selling his gym-launch playbook to gym owners, which showed him how elastic his pricing was. He also covers how to judge an opportunity, how to narrow a market, hiring on character, why skills compound, and what a brand is.

principles.text: Judge an opportunity on three variables: market size, value-to-cost gap, and competitive dynamics. Look for all three.
principles.quote: i see it as three variables so you have uh the total number of potential units to sell

principles.text: Narrow to your best customers. Find what the top 20% have in common and sell only to that group, with no extra operational drag.
principles.quote: what if we only sold that amount of people and we sold now the same hundred but they were all of that 20 percent right well we would 5x our revenue

principles.text: Test price elasticity by raising the price. Each higher quote kept closing, which exposed how underpriced the offer was.
principles.quote: next guy how much eight grand next time how much 10 grand next and then i did 60 000 in sales that day

principles.text: Hire on character before skill. His three values are unimpeachable character, sincere candor and competitive greatness, in that order.
principles.quote: unimpeachable character sincere candor and competitive greatness and so those are the only three things and we look for them pretty much in that order

principles.text: Skills are the asset that keeps appreciating and stacking, whatever the economy or currency does.
principles.quote: skills are the only thing that will always appreciate in time

principles.text: A brand is reputation, meaning what people say about you when you're not there. You build it from the inside out.
principles.quote: i see brand as reputation and i see reputation as what people say about you when you're not there so that is your brand
